name.text: Finding integers for a logarithmic equation

questiontext.text:
Solve the logarithmic equation:

\(\log_{@b@}(x+{@a@})=\log_{@b@}(2x-{@c@})+1\)

Enter your answer for \(x\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To solve the logarithmic equation, use the logarithm law:

\(\log_b(A)+1=\log_b(bA)\).

The original equation is:

\(\log_{@b@}(x+{@a@})=\log_{@b@}(2x-{@c@})+1\)

Rewrite the right-hand side using the logarithm law:

\(\log_{@b@}(x+{@a@})=\log_{@b@}\bigl(@b@(2x-{@c@})\bigr)\)

Since the logarithms have the same base, their arguments must be equal:

\(x+{@a@}=@b@(2x-{@c@})\)

Expand the brackets:

\(x+{@a@}=2{@b@}x-{@b@}{@c@}\)

Rearrange to collect the terms containing \(x\):

\(x+{@a@}{+}{@b@}{@c@}=2{@b@}x\)

\({@a@}+{@b@}{@c@}=(2{@b@}-1)x\)

Divide by \(2{@b@}-1\):

\(x=\frac{@a@+{@b@}{@c@}}{2{@b@}-1}\)

By the construction of the Question Variables, the correct answer is:

\(\boxed{x={@ans@}}\)

Finally, check the domain restrictions. Both logarithm arguments must be positive:

\(x+{@a@}>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad 2x-{@c@}>0.\)

A solution is valid only if both conditions are satisfied.
